headline: Rates Hold Near 1-Month Lows as Oil Eases Into Fed Week
tileReason: The daily 30-year average ticked up to 7.33% Friday but stays near a one-month low, and easing oil prices are giving bonds a slight lift this morning ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision.
takeaway: Mortgage rates barely moved to end last week. The daily 30-year average edged up 0.03% to 7.33% on Friday, giving back a sliver of Thursday's big drop but staying close to its lowest level in a month. Tech stocks calmed down on Friday, so less money rushed into the safety of bonds, and the 10-year Treasury yield rose back to about 5.00% from 4.96%. This morning the picture is a little friendlier. Oil prices are down about 1% to 2% (Brent crude near $114 to $115 a barrel) after Iran signaled it is open to restarting talks with Saudi Arabia and others, and President Trump said no strike on Iran was coming immediately. Cheaper oil eases inflation worries, and the 10-year yield has slipped to roughly 4.97% to 4.99%. That usually points to flat to slightly better pricing from lenders today. The big events are later this week: the Federal Reserve (the Fed, the central bank) decides on rates Wednesday, and the inflation measure it watches most closely, PCE, comes out Thursday along with the first estimate of third-quarter economic growth. Markets see about a 90% chance the Fed holds steady Wednesday, but roughly a 75% to 80% chance of a hike in December, so Chair Warsh's comments could move rates either way. Over the next month the odds look roughly balanced, with a slight lean toward rates staying about where they are.

fedOdds.title: Odds of a Fed hike on Oct 28
fedOdds.source: CME FedWatch via FXEmpire (Oct 26, morning) and Trading Economics (Oct 23–26); Schwab via Vantage Markets (Oct 23)
fedOdds.note: CME FedWatch showed about a 91% chance the Fed holds on October 28 this morning, so roughly 9% for a hike (FXEmpire, citing FedWatch, Oct 26); Schwab put hike odds near 8% on Friday, and Kitco says about 90% for a hold. December is a different story: FedWatch shows about 72% for one quarter-point hike plus about 7% for two, so roughly 80% for at least one, versus about 76% in Trading Economics' Friday reading and about 84% for a hike by year-end in Schwab's Friday read. The Fed is in its quiet period before the meeting, so no official comments are expected.

drivers.title: Oil pulls back on hopes for Gulf talks
drivers.text: Oil fell about 1% to 2% this morning, with Brent crude near $114 to $115 a barrel after settling around $116.70 on Friday, its highest since 2022. Iran signaled it is willing to restart talks, Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials are expected in Tehran, and President Trump said there would be no strike on Iran right away. Cheaper energy eases inflation fears, so bond investors accept slightly lower yields, which helps mortgage rates. Houthi attacks on Saudi targets are continuing, so this relief could reverse quickly.

drivers.title: Tech stocks steady, so the bond rally pauses
drivers.text: Thursday's tech selloff sent money into bonds and pulled rates to a one-month low. On Friday tech stocks calmed and the Nasdaq edged up, so some of that safe-haven money left bonds. When fewer investors are buying bonds, yields rise: the 10-year Treasury yield climbed back to about 5.00% and the daily 30-year mortgage average ticked up 0.03%. Big tech companies report earnings this week, so this tug-of-war may continue.

drivers.title: Fed meets Wednesday with a December hike in view
drivers.text: Markets expect the Fed to hold its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday, but they see roughly a 75% to 80% chance of a hike in December after hot September inflation. That expectation keeps a floor under bond yields and mortgage rates. If Chair Warsh sounds more worried about inflation than expected, rates could rise; if he sounds patient, they could ease.

drivers.title: Inflation and growth data due Thursday
drivers.text: Thursday brings the PCE price index, the inflation measure the Fed watches most closely, plus the first estimate of third-quarter growth (GDP). September consumer prices already came in hotter than forecast, so investors are bracing for firm numbers. That caution makes bond buyers a bit hesitant ahead of the release.

drivers.title: Mortgage rates are still unusually far above Treasuries
drivers.text: The daily 30-year average is running about 2.3% above the 10-year Treasury yield, compared with a more typical 2.0%. That extra cushion means mortgage rates have room to improve if markets calm down, even without a further drop in Treasury yields.

outlook.basis: It's close to a coin flip, with a slight lean toward rates staying about where they are. Working in borrowers' favor: oil is backing off its 2022-level highs on talk of Gulf diplomacy, nervous tech stocks can send money into bonds on short notice, and mortgage rates are still unusually far above the 10-year Treasury (about 2.3% vs. a typical 2.0%). Working against them: a December Fed hike is still widely expected, September inflation ran hot, and oil remains above $100 with attacks on Saudi targets continuing. Big swing events: the October 28 Fed decision, the October 29 PCE inflation and GDP data, the November 3 midterm elections, the November 6 jobs report, the November 10 CPI report, and any escalation in the Gulf.
outlook.caveat: This is professional judgment from 30+ years watching these markets, not a guarantee. One oil headline or data surprise can move rates a quarter point in a day.

talkingPoints.buyers: The daily 30-year average is about 7.33%, close to a one-month low and down from roughly 7.5% in early October. The Fed decides Wednesday and key inflation data lands Thursday, so this week could bring bigger swings than usual; it's worth asking your lender how locking now, a float-down option, or waiting would each fit your closing date.
talkingPoints.sellers: Rates have eased from early-October highs, but buyers are still stretched and careful. Realistic pricing, or a seller credit buyers can use to buy down their rate, can help your home stand out while rates sit near a one-month low.
talkingPoints.oneLiner: Mortgage rates are holding near a one-month low around 7.33%, with oil easing this morning, but the Fed's Wednesday decision and Thursday's inflation data could shake things up.
